title: Brutalist Concrete Office Slab

front: A two-point street view from the south-east corner with upright verticals. A fitted camera (2.4 m eye height, 40 degree lens, vertical shift) puts six measured corners within 10 px on the 1024 px image.

Down the south-east corner edge: 230 px of clear ground storey, four pairs of 108 px ribbon and 107 px band, and a 115 px top band. At the variant's 3.9 m storey this gives a 4.1 m clear ground storey, 1.95 m ribbons and bands, and a parapet at 21.9 m.
Ground storey plus four office storeys: five. The catalogue text says six; the selected-variant images govern.
Five structural bays across the street front, marked by band joints and granite piers about 1.3 m wide, with six window modules to a bay.
Each band carries a cap strip about 0.5 m tall that projects beyond the main face and throws a shadow line. The glass sits about 0.5 m behind the cap.
One pair of glazed entrance doors in the second bay from the east corner, with a transom at door-head height. Timber panelling shows through the corner bay.
East flank at street level: the glazing returns a short way, then blank granite between piers, with a service door at the far end.
The walkway leaves the east flank at the third storey, its glazing level with that storey's ribbon, under a rounded concrete crown and over a rounded belly.
oblique: A fitted camera (44 m up to the south-east, 39 degree lens) puts seven measured corners within 16 px on the 1195 px image.
Four ribbon storeys over the ground storey on both visible sides, with band joints at the structural lines.
Penthouse about 7.3 m tall in board-formed panels roughly 2.25 m wide with one horizontal joint; a door and a louvre on its east face; an open well in its rear east corner.
Flat gravel roof inside a concrete parapet with a bronze flashing on its inner edge.
top: Footprint 670 px by 615 px, a ratio of 1.09. Built 45.0 m by 40.5 m, a ratio of 1.11.
Penthouse 337 px by 343 px, centred, about 9 m from every parapet. Built 22.5 m square, centred.
Open well about 8 m square in the penthouse's rear east corner holding one square unit.
Walkway 4.4 m wide on the east flank, centred about 29 percent of the depth back from the street corner. Built 4.5 m wide on the window module, centred 11.25 m back.
Roof items: one hatch south of the penthouse, one vent to its east, one unit and two conduit runs on its roof.

source_conflicts: Walkway level. The archetype text places +15 walkways at the second storey; both perspective sources show this one at the third. Built as drawn, floor 9.1 m above grade.

Penthouse from the street. The street view shows about 6 m of penthouse above the parapet line. The roof plan and the oblique, which agree with each other, cannot produce that from the fitted street camera; about 1 m shows. Roof plan and oblique govern.
Storey count. The catalogue description says six storeys; both perspective sources show five.
hidden_assumptions: The west flank and the rear are not shown. The west flank mirrors the east at street level, with plant louvres and an exit door. The rear is a service side with high windows, a loading door and a staff exit. The ribbon bands repeat on all four sides above.
Interior layout, floor levels behind the bands and the structural grid are inferred from the facade rhythm.
The walkway runs on to a neighbouring building in the sources. It is delivered as a 9 m length with a glazed end, no neighbour and no support at the free end.
The penthouse's rear and west faces are plain board-formed panels.
